title: Antioxidant‐functionalized quantum dots mitigate cadmium toxicity and enhance grain quality and yield in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) cultivars
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Cadmium (Cd) contamination limits wheat productivity and grain quality by disrupting growth, photosynthesis, redox homeostasis, and nutrient allocation. This study evaluated the effectiveness of ascorbate-, glutathione-, and berberine-functionalized quantum dots (ASCQDs, GLUQDs, and BERQDs) in mitigating Cd toxicity in two bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) cultivars, ‘SKD-1’ and ‘Borlaug-16’, grown in soil containing 50 mg kg−1 Cd.

RESULTS

Cadmium exposure altered phenological, physiological, oxidative, antioxidant, and grain biochemical responses, with considerable variation between cultivars. Antioxidant-functionalized quantum dots (QDs) modulated chlorophyll and carotenoid profiles, reduced oxidative damage under certain treatments, and altered enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidant responses, including those of superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), proline, ascorbate, glutathione-related metabolites, phenolics, and flavonoids. Quantum dot treatments also modified Cd accumulation and partitioning among soil, roots, leaves, and available grain samples, although the magnitude and direction of these effects depended on cultivar and QD formulation. Agronomic responses were similarly treatment-specific, with combined Cd + QD treatments not consistently improving performance. Cultivar-specific principal component analysis (PCA) distinguished treatment responses, with the first two principal components (PC1 and PC2) explaining a cumulative 55.3% of the variation in ‘SKD-1’ and 47.6% in ‘Borlaug-16’.

CONCLUSION

Antioxidant-functionalized QDs modulated several components of the wheat response to Cd stress, particularly redox regulation, thiol metabolism, photosynthetic adjustment, and Cd partitioning. Their effectiveness depended strongly on QD formulation and wheat genotype, highlighting the need for further optimization of functionalized QDs for Cd stress management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
